## The three names in the question

**Voicebox** (`jamiepine/voicebox`, read): "The open-source AI voice
studio" — "Clone any voice. Generate speech. Dictate into any app. Talk to
agents in voices you own." A local-first desktop app (Tauri, Rust backend)
for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows, Linux and Docker. Seven TTS
engines: Qwen3-TTS, Qwen CustomVoice, LuxTTS, Chatterbox Multilingual,
Chatterbox Turbo, HumeAI TADA, Kokoro. Speech-to-text is OpenAI Whisper "on
MLX (Apple Silicon) or PyTorch (CUDA / ROCm / DirectML / CPU)", Base to
Large and Turbo. A bundled local LLM — Qwen3 at 0.6B, 1.7B or 4B — rewrites
dictation and applies per-profile personas. An MCP server lets "any
MCP-aware AI agent" (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) speak in a chosen
voice. MIT. *(search)* 43,000-plus GitHub stars by mid-2026. It is a voice
*studio* and a dictation tool with an agent bridge — not a conversational
agent on its own; the conversation partner is whatever MCP client calls it.

**VoiceStudio** (`debpalash/VoiceStudio`, read 2026-09-14; "Previously
OmniVoice-Studio"): "Clone voices, dub video, dictate, and produce
long-form audio on your own hardware." "16 TTS engines · 11 ASR engines ·
646-language catalogue · macOS, Windows, Linux, and Docker." "No account,
API key, subscription, or usage meter for the local workflow." GitHub
description: "the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative."
Created 2026-04-09; 27,151 stars and 3,344 forks on 2026-09-14; last push
2026-09-11. Architecture: "Tauri v2 desktop shell (Rust)" → "React + Vite
UI" → "FastAPI backend" on `localhost:3900` with "TTS / ASR engine
registries", "OpenAI-compatible API and MCP server", "SQLite + Alembic".
The README's first line: "NOTE: Electron Rewrite Ongoing"; a warning box:
"Active beta."

TTS engines listed: VoiceStudio default "powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice"
(600+ languages, "Apache-2.0 code, CC-BY-NC weights", audio tokenizer
"under separate Boson Higgs Audio 2 and Meta Llama community terms"),
CosyVoice 3, GPT-SoVITS, VoxCPM2, MOSS-TTS-Nano, KittenTTS, MLX-Audio,
Sherpa-ONNX, IndexTTS 2.5 (Bilibili model licence), OmniVoice GGUF,
OmniVoice subprocess, PocketTTS ("CC-BY-4.0, gated"), Supertonic 3
(OpenRAIL-M), MOSS-TTS-v1.5, dots.tts, Confucius4-TTS. ASR engines:
WhisperX (default), Faster-Whisper (and an isolated variant), MLX Whisper,
PyTorch Whisper, Parakeet TDT (NeMo and MLX), Moonshine, FunASR,
sherpa-onnx "live dictation", and an OpenAI-compatible ASR server
("Local gigastt/Qwen3-ASR or a remote endpoint"). Hardware table:
"Low VRAM / CPU-only" → PocketTTS, Sherpa-ONNX, KittenTTS for TTS and
Moonshine, Faster-Whisper int8 for ASR. Requirements: 8 GB RAM minimum,
"GPU: Optional; CPU mode is supported"; Intel Macs "cannot run the local
Python backend."

Features: voice cloning ("Three seconds works; 5 to 15 seconds usually
gives a better prompt"), voice design from a description, video dubbing
("Transcribe, translate, preserve speakers, synthesize, and export
video"), stories and audiobooks with `.m4b` export, "Dictation Widget:
System-wide shortcut, live transcription, optional local-LLM cleanup",
Demucs vocal isolation, Pyannote/WhisperX diarization, batch queue,
AudioSeal watermarking, remote workers. Agent side: MCP server at
`http://localhost:3900/mcp` with tools `generate_speech`, `clone_voice`,
`transcribe`; OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/speech` and
`/v1/audio/transcriptions`; `WS /v1/audio/transcriptions/stream` for
"Live PCM/WebM transcription with partial, utterance, and session-final
events"; `npx skills add debpalash/VoiceStudio` for "Claude Code, Codex,
Cursor". Network boundary: "loopback-only backend", "Analytics is off
until consent."

Licence: application AGPL-3.0 (`LICENSE`, read); "downloaded models keep
their upstream terms." Same category as Voicebox — a studio and a
dictation tool with an agent bridge, not a conversational agent — with a
longer engine list, a wider API surface, and a copyleft licence.

**VoxCPM** (`OpenBMB/VoxCPM`, read): "VoxCPM2 is a tokenizer-free
Text-to-Speech system that directly generates continuous speech
representations via an end-to-end diffusion autoregressive architecture."
From the MiniCPM team at OpenBMB. Three generations: VoxCPM-0.5B (September
2025, "legacy"), VoxCPM1.5 (0.6B, December 2025, "stable"), VoxCPM2 (2B,
April 2026). Four stages — LocEnc, TSLM, RALM, LocDiT — in the latent space
of an AudioVAE, so there is no discrete speech tokenizer; 30 languages plus
nine Chinese dialects; 48 kHz output from 16 kHz references; Voice Design
from a text description, controllable cloning, "Ultimate Cloning" from audio
plus transcript. "Weights and code released under the Apache-2.0 license,
free for commercial use." Real-time factor "as low as ~0.3 on RTX 4090;
~0.13 with Nano-vLLM"; streaming inference supported. `pip install voxcpm`
(2.0.3 on PyPI). It is a TTS model — the mouth, not the brain — and a GPU
one at 2B.

**Dograh** (`dograh-hq/dograh`, read): "The open-source, self-hostable
alternative to Vapi & Retell" — a platform for building telephone and
browser voice agents with a visual workflow builder (start nodes, agent
nodes, global instructions, tools, transitions, end-call outcomes), a test
panel in audio or text, an MCP server so coding agents can build workflows,
and telephony through Twilio, Vonage, Telnyx, Plivo, Vobiz, Cloudonix and
Asterisk ARI. "On Prem, BYOK across Speech to Speech or LLM/STT/TTS." One
Docker command; BSD 2-Clause. Its `docker-compose.yaml` (read) runs
Postgres, Redis, MinIO, nginx, coturn, an API and a UI container and
Cloudflare's tunnel — no speech model and no LLM container. "Ships with
auto-generated keys and its own LLM / TTS / STT stack" therefore means a
hosted default, with your own providers as the local path; whether that
stack can be pointed at a machine in the room depends on the provider list,
which was not readable (docs blocked). It is orchestration, not a model.

## Three shapes

Every local voice agent is one of three things, and the choice decides the
hardware.

**1. The cascade — STT → LLM → TTS.** Three models, three latencies added
together, but each replaceable and the LLM any text model you already run.
Unmute, Pipecat, LiveKit Agents, Dograh, Bolna, Speaches, Home Assistant's
Assist pipeline, Voicebox's dictation loop and the RealtimeSTT/RealtimeTTS
pair are all this. Latency comes from streaming every stage and detecting
the end of the user's turn early.

**2. Speech-native, half-duplex.** One model hears audio and speaks audio
through a "Thinker–Talker" or similar split, but still takes turns:
Qwen3-Omni and Qwen3.5-Omni, MiniCPM-o (half-duplex mode), Step-Audio 2,
Kimi-Audio, GLM-4-Voice. Ultravox is half of this (speech in, text out) and
Sesame's CSM the other half (text and audio context in, speech out).

**3. Full-duplex.** The model listens while it speaks — interruptions,
back-channels, overlap — from one network: Moshi (Kyutai, 2024), NVIDIA's
PersonaPlex (January 2026, built on Moshi), MiniCPM-o 4.5 in full-duplex
mode. The rarest, the most natural, and the most GPU-bound.

## Shape 1 — the cascade

**Unmute** (`kyutai-labs/unmute`, read): "a system that allows text LLMs to
listen and speak by wrapping them in Kyutai's Text-to-speech and
Speech-to-text models." Kyutai STT, any LLM served by vLLM or OpenRouter,
Kyutai TTS, a Rust backend, a web frontend; Docker Compose; "a GPU with CUDA
support and at least 16 GB VRAM. Architecture must be x86_64." TTS latency
"decreases from ~750ms when running everything on a single L40S GPU to
around ~450ms" with a GPU per service. MIT. *(search)* Kyutai's own figure:
the TTS "can serve 32 users with a 350ms latency on a single L40S", and the
whole response "is below a second."

**Kyutai STT and TTS** (`delayed-streams-modeling`, read): streaming
sequence-to-sequence models built on "Delayed Streams Modeling". STT in two
sizes — 1B (English and French, "0.5 second delay") and 2.6B (English, "2.5
second delay") — with word timestamps and a semantic VAD; TTS 1.6B at about
220 ms; PyTorch, MLX for Apple silicon "(iPhone/Mac)", a Rust server that
on an H100 can "process 400 streams in real-time". Code MIT and Apache;
STT weights CC-BY 4.0.

**Pipecat** (`pipecat-ai/pipecat`, read; 1.10.0 on PyPI, 12 September
2026): "an open-source Python framework for building real-time voice and
multimodal conversational agents." Maintained by Daily. Services by
category, with the local ones named: STT — Whisper locally (plus a dozen
APIs); LLM — Ollama locally; TTS — Kokoro and Piper locally; speech-to-speech
— AWS Nova Sonic, Gemini Multimodal Live, OpenAI Realtime, Ultravox; VAD —
Silero; transport — Daily, LiveKit, WebSocket, local. The PyPI extras add
`pocket-tts`, `mlx-whisper`, `moonshine`, `local-smart-turn`. `uv tool
install "pipecat-ai[cli]"; pipecat init quickstart`.

**Smart Turn** (`pipecat-ai/smart-turn`, read): semantic end-of-turn
detection — "when a voice agent should respond to human speech" — v3.2,
"Whisper Tiny as a base, with a linear classifier layer", about 8M
parameters, "Runs in as little as 10ms on some CPUs", 23 languages; "The
datasets, training script, and model weights are all open source" under BSD
2-Clause; `LocalSmartTurnAnalyzerV3` in Pipecat.

**LiveKit Agents** (`livekit/agents`, read; 1.8.1 on PyPI): "realtime,
programmable participants that run on servers", "a comprehensive ecosystem
to mix and match the right STT, LLM, TTS, and Realtime API"; "Fully
open-source, allowing you to run the entire stack on your own servers,
including LiveKit server". Apache-2.0 framework; the **turn detector** —
"a custom open-weight model" that "requires <500MB of RAM" and "runs on CPUs
with modest system requirements" — is under "the LiveKit Model License".
Silero VAD as a plugin. Provider plugins are mostly cloud (Deepgram,
Cartesia, OpenAI); local STT and TTS go through OpenAI-compatible servers
such as Speaches.

**Speaches** (`speaches-ai/speaches`, read): "OpenAI API-compatible server
supporting streaming transcription, translation, and speech generation" —
faster-whisper for STT, Kokoro and Piper for TTS, a Realtime API, "GPU and
CPU support", Docker. MIT. The adapter that lets any framework speaking
OpenAI's API use local models.

**Bolna** (`bolna-ai/bolna`, read): "the end-to-end open source production
ready framework for quickly building LLM based voice driven conversational
applications"; STT via Deepgram and Azure, TTS via Polly, ElevenLabs,
Cartesia and others, telephony via Twilio and Plivo, LLMs including "hosted
via VLLM". MIT. Cloud-first, with the LLM the one local slot.

**Home Assistant's Assist pipeline** — the largest deployed local voice
stack, and the one that runs on a $59 device. **Wyoming**
(`OHF-Voice/wyoming`, read): "A peer-to-peer TCP protocol for voice
assistants (basically JSONL + PCM audio)", "An open standard from the Open
Home Foundation", spoken by wake-word services (openWakeWord, Porcupine,
Snowboy, microWakeWord), STT (Faster Whisper, Vosk, whisper.cpp), TTS
(Piper) and satellites. **Speech-to-Phrase** (read): "a fast and local
speech-to-text system that is personalized with your Home Assistant device
and area names" — "Instead of answering the question 'what did the user
say?', it answers 'which of the phrases I know did the user say?'"; 21
languages; the trick that makes a Raspberry Pi 4 usable. **Piper**
(`OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl`, read): "A fast and local neural text-to-speech
engine that embeds espeak-ng for phonemization"; GPL-3.0-or-later on PyPI
(1.8.0, 4 September 2026). **microWakeWord** (read): "an open-source
wakeword library for detecting custom wake words on low power devices",
producing TensorFlow Lite Micro models; ESPHome and Nabu Casa in the
acknowledgements. *(search)* **Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition**: $59;
ESP32-S3 with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM; an XMOS XU316 for echo
cancellation, noise removal and gain; dual microphones, a speaker and a
3.5 mm jack, a hardware mute switch, a rotary dial; wake word on the device
with microWakeWord; the rest over Wi-Fi to the Home Assistant server, for
which "an Intel N100 or higher is recommended" for fully local speech.
The 2026 community stack: openWakeWord or microWakeWord, Whisper, Home
Assistant's intent system or Ollama with a Qwen3, Piper or Kokoro.

## Shape 2 — speech-native, taking turns

**Qwen3-Omni** (`QwenLM/Qwen3-Omni`, read): "natively end-to-end
multilingual omni-modal foundation models" that "process text, images,
audio, and video, while delivering real-time streaming responses in both
text and natural speech." Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B in Instruct (speech out),
Thinking and Captioner variants; "MoE-based Thinker–Talker design", "211ms"
end-to-end audio latency; 119 text languages, 19 speech in, 10 speech out.
GPU memory in bf16: "78.85GB (15s video) to 144.81GB (120s video)" for
Instruct. Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`, read). *(search)* **Qwen3.5-Omni** (30
March 2026): the same 30B/3B-active shape with web search and function
calling from the omni model, with downloadable weights; Qwen2.5-Omni-3B
remains the small one.

**MiniCPM-o 4.5** (`OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o`, read): 9B, "end-to-end omnimodal
interaction with streaming video and audio inputs plus text and speech
outputs"; "full-duplex multimodal live streaming" where "output streams
(speech and text), and the real-time input streams (video and audio) do not
block each other"; full duplex needs "Apple M4 Max chip with at least 24GB
RAM or low-resource Nvidia GPU with at least 12GB GPU memory", half-duplex
speech "Apple M3/M4/M5 chip with at least 16GB RAM"; voice cloning and
role-play from a reference clip; open-sourced 2026-02-03; code Apache-2.0
(`LICENSE`, read; model terms not read). The only omni model in this list
whose stated floor is a laptop.

**Step-Audio 2** (`stepfun-ai/Step-Audio2`, read): "an end-to-end
multi-modal large language model designed for industry-strength audio
understanding and speech conversation"; open models Step-Audio 2 mini, mini
Base and mini Think (29 August and 15 September 2025); tool calling, RAG and
web search; GPU with vLLM; Apache 2.0. **Kimi-Audio** (`MoonshotAI/Kimi-Audio`,
read): 7B, "audio understanding, generation, and conversation" in one
model, on Qwen2.5-7B; April 2025; code Apache-2.0 and MIT; weight terms not
stated in the README. **Ultravox** (`fixie-ai/ultravox`, read): "a fast
multimodal LLM designed for real-time voice interactions" that understands
"human speech, without the need for a separate Audio Speech Recognition
(ASR) stage" — on Llama 3.3 70B and 8B, v0.7 of December 2025; "currently
takes in audio and emits streaming text", so a TTS finishes the job.
**Sesame CSM** (`SesameAILabs/csm`, read): "a speech generation model from
Sesame that generates RVQ audio codes from text and audio inputs", "a Llama
backbone and a smaller audio decoder that produces Mimi audio codes"; 1B;
Apache 2.0; a CUDA GPU; "not a general-purpose multimodal LLM" — pair it
with one. *(search)* Sesame's demo voices, Maya and Miles, run on an 8B that
was not released.

## Shape 3 — full duplex

**Moshi** (`kyutai-labs/moshi`, read): "a speech-text foundation model and
full-duplex spoken dialogue framework" on Mimi, a codec taking "24 kHz audio
down to 12.5 Hz" at "1.1 kbps" with "latency of 80ms". A 7B Temporal
Transformer; "160ms (80ms for the frame size of Mimi + 80ms of acoustic
delay)" theoretical latency, "~200ms on L4 GPU" in practice. Three
implementations: PyTorch (24 GB VRAM unquantised), MLX for M-series Macs
(q4, q8, bf16), Rust for production (int8, bf16). `pip install -U moshi`,
`python -m moshi.server`; `pip install -U moshi_mlx`, `python -m
moshi_mlx.local -q 4`. Code MIT and Apache; weights CC-BY 4.0. The one
full-duplex model that documents a Mac.

**PersonaPlex** (`NVIDIA/personaplex`, read): "a real-time, full-duplex
speech-to-speech conversational model that enables persona control through
text-based role prompts and audio-based voice conditioning"; 7B; "based on
the Moshi architecture and weights" with "the underlying Helium LLM"; a
`--cpu-offload` flag for small GPUs; code MIT, weights NVIDIA Open Model
License. *(search)* Released 2026-01-20; interruption latency "as low as
240 milliseconds"; ports to Apple silicon via MLX exist.

## The parts, when you assemble your own

**Speech-to-text.** Whisper is still the default through three runtimes —
whisper.cpp (`pywhispercpp` 1.5.1), CTranslate2 (`faster-whisper` 1.2.1),
MLX (`mlx-whisper` 0.4.3) — and large-v3-turbo the usual size. *(search)*
The 2026 alternatives: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT (0.6B, RTFx above 2,000 on a GPU,
CC-BY) and Canary-Qwen 2.5B for English accuracy; **Moonshine**
(`usefulsensors/moonshine`, read: "an open source AI toolkit for developers
building real-time voice agents", "Everything runs on-device", MIT, "tiny
1MB models", streaming, higher accuracy than Whisper Large V3 claimed for
2026 models); **Kyutai STT** (above); **Voxtral Realtime** — Mistral, 4
February 2026, "Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602", Apache 2.0, configurable
delay from 80 ms to 2.4 s, Whisper-level accuracy at 480 ms, 16 GB of VRAM
or a 2.5 GB Q4 build in a browser via WebGPU; **Qwen3-ASR** (30 January
2026, 0.6B and 1.7B, 52 languages and dialects, Apache 2.0); Microsoft's
**VibeVoice-ASR** (7B, January 2026; a streaming variant September 2026);
and **Gemma 3n**, whose USM-based audio encoder makes "a token for every
160ms of audio" so a 2–4 GB open model transcribes and understands speech
in one pass.

**Text-to-speech, smallest first.** **Kitten TTS** (`KittenML/KittenTTS`,
read): "an open-source, lightweight text-to-speech library built on ONNX",
15M, 40M and 80M parameters, "runs efficiently without a GPU", Apache 2.0.
**Kokoro** (`hexgrad/kokoro`, read): "an open-weight TTS model with 82
million parameters", Apache-licensed weights, nine language variants;
`kokoro-onnx` for CPU. **Pocket TTS** (`kyutai-labs/pocket-tts`, read): "A
lightweight text-to-speech (TTS) application designed to run efficiently on
CPUs", 100M parameters, "~6x real-time on a CPU of MacBook Air M4", "~200ms
to get the first audio chunk", six languages, voice cloning from a WAV,
MIT; training code released August 2026. **Piper** (above; GPL).
**Chatterbox** (`resemble-ai/chatterbox`, read): "a family of
state-of-the-art, open-source text-to-speech models by Resemble AI" — 0.5B
base, Multilingual V3 (23-plus languages), **Turbo** (350M, "for
low-latency voice agents"), **Nano** (110M, "runs on CPU at 3x faster than
realtime on 8 cores"); an "exaggeration" dial; PerTh watermarking in every
output; MIT. **LuxTTS** *(search; repository fetch failed)*: ZipVoice-based
cloning at 48 kHz, "150x realtime" on a GPU and faster than real time on
CPUs, under 1 GB. **Qwen3-TTS** (`QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS`, read): 0.6B and 1.7B
in Base, CustomVoice and VoiceDesign flavours on a 12 Hz tokenizer,
"first-packet latency as low as 97ms", 10 languages, streaming, Apache 2.0,
22 January 2026. **VoxCPM2** (above; 2B, GPU). **TADA** (`HumeAI/tada`,
read): "a unified speech-language model that synchronizes speech and text
into a single, cohesive stream via 1:1 alignment" — TADA-1B and TADA-3B-ML on
Llama 3.2, so weights under the Llama 3.2 Community License, code MIT;
March 2026. **VibeVoice** (`microsoft/VibeVoice`, read): TTS 1.5B for
"speech up to 90 minutes long with up to 4 distinct speakers", **Realtime
0.5B** at "~300 milliseconds first audible latency" (December 2025), MIT.
**Orpheus** (`canopyai/Orpheus-TTS`, read): "built on the Llama-3b
backbone", "~200ms streaming latency", emotive tags, a llama.cpp path for
no-GPU use. **Dia** (`nari-labs/dia`, read): 1.6B dialogue with `[S1]`/`[S2]`
tags and non-verbals, about 4.4 GB of VRAM, "CPU support has not yet been
implemented", Apache 2.0. **Fish Audio S2 Pro** (`fishaudio/fish-speech`,
read): 4B, 80-plus languages, "FISH AUDIO RESEARCH LICENSE" for code and
weights — not open for commercial use.

**Turn-taking and wake words.** **Silero VAD** (`snakers4/silero-vad`,
read): "Pre-trained enterprise-grade Voice Activity Detector", about 2 MB,
"One audio chunk (30+ ms) takes less than 1ms to be processed on a single
CPU thread", "over 6000 languages", MIT; 6.2.1 on PyPI. **Smart Turn** and
the **LiveKit turn detector** (above). **openWakeWord** (`dscripka/openWakeWord`,
read): "an open-source wakeword library"; pre-trained "alexa, hey mycroft,
hey jarvis, hey rhasspy, timers, and current weather"; "<0.5/hour
false-accept rates"; "A single core of a Raspberry Pi 3 can run 15-20
openWakeWord models simultaneously in real-time"; "trained with 100%
synthetic speech generated from text-to-speech models"; code Apache 2.0,
pre-trained models CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0 — the one non-commercial licence in the
household stack. **microWakeWord** (above) for the ESP32.

**Runtimes.** **sherpa-onnx** (`k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx`, read; 1.13.8): runs
"locally" streaming and offline STT, TTS, VAD, keyword spotting, speaker
diarisation and enhancement; Zipformer, Whisper, Moonshine, SenseVoice and
Paraformer for STT, Piper, Kokoro and Matcha for TTS, Silero for VAD; on
Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, Raspberry Pi and RISC-V
boards, WebAssembly and several NPUs; bindings in twelve languages; Apache
2.0. The engine the CPU run below used.

## The closed baselines *(search)*

OpenAI's gpt-realtime: one model, audio in and out, "$32 per 1M audio input
tokens and $64 per 1M audio output tokens" after a 20% cut, about 800 ms
voice-to-voice when configured well. Google's Gemini Live API: native audio
in and out, "30 HD voices in 24 languages". Both are what Dograh, Pipecat
and LiveKit call "speech-to-speech" providers; neither runs in the room.
